newsitem.title: FRANCE: France warns against use of force by Bosnian Serbs.
newsitem.headline: France warns against use of force by Bosnian Serbs.

text.p: France warned opponents of the Bosnian Serb government on Friday not to resort to force in a confrontation over the president's authority to dissolve the assembly and set new elections.
"We warn against the use of force, in the face of which the international community would be unable to remain passive," French Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt said.

He said Bosnian Serb President Biljana Plavsic's decision taken on Thursday to dissolve the assembly was constitutional and must be respected by other Bosnian Serb entities. Plavsic set new elections for September 1.
The government of Bosnia's Serb territory, dominated behind the scenes by indicted war criminal and wartime leader Radovan Karadzic, has dismissed the president's move as unconstitutional.
It prepared to go ahead with an assembly session on Friday called to launch the removal of Plavsic as president.

On the eve of the assembly, government hardliners shut down the official television station in the northern town of Banja Luka, the power base for Plavsic who has accused the ruling party of growing rich off war profiteering.
